Spotlight engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Spotlight capability covers storefront language. Xcode, Developer portal, and Connect actually separate in-app search indexing from product-page copy:

  • CoreSpotlight & CSSearchableItem — configured in your app to donate searchable records and attributes. Controls whether your content appears in on-device Spotlight results. Does not generate Chinese listing text. AppLocale does not implement this.
  • NSUserActivity & Siri Suggestions donation — activity types and prediction signals that surface your app in Siri Suggestions from Spotlight. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Spotlight value to buyers.
  • In-app search UI & result labels — search bars, filters, and result row titles on your screens. Your listing may mention Find it instantly; implementing searchable-item indexing is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Spotlight indexing in the binary.

Working Spotlight surfacing in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Spotlight-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Discovery-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe on-device search — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Search with Spotlight vs Find it instantly vs Spotlight Search

US pages use "Search with Spotlight", "Find it instantly", "Spotlight Search", or "find it in Spotlight." Chinese buyers expect concise 聚焦搜索, 系统搜索, Spotlight搜索, or 下拉搜索 phrasing rather than English slogans left on screenshot overlays — without implying you are the built-in Search app or index every file type on the device.

Siri Suggestions from Spotlight vs App Intents marketing

Some listings reference Siri Suggestions chips that appear when users pull down Search — predictive shortcuts tied to donated activities. That is different from Ask Siri to… voice-action marketing or Shortcuts app tile screenshots. Chinese buyers expect distinct vocabulary (Siri建议, 聚焦搜索建议) rather than conflating Siri Suggestions with App Intents action phrases.

On-device discovery vs App Store Search

Spotlight marketing describes finding content inside or via your app from the system search surface — not ranking higher in the App Store search results tab. Listing copy should not blur on-device Spotlight discovery with App Store Optimization keyword stuffing or paid Apple Search Ads placement.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Spotlight-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 聚焦搜索, 系统搜索, and Spotlight搜索 each signal different intent from generic utility keywords.

Screenshot captions on Spotlight frames

Gallery frames that show pull-down iOS Search, Spotlight result rows, Siri Suggestions chips, or find-it-in-Spotlight onboarding need one-line zh-Hans captions — "下拉搜索，聚焦搜索即刻找到" not "Search with Spotlight" burned into the product page story.

Common mistakes on Spotlight zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Spotlight indexing localizes automatically — CSSearchableItem or NSUserActivity wired in Xcode; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and Spotlight-themed screenshot caption lines still English
  • Conflating Spotlight with App Intents or Siri Shortcuts — voice action phrases and Shortcuts tiles use different buyer vocabulary; see App Intents listing guide and spoken App Shortcut phrases guide, not this page
  • Conflating Spotlight with Apple Search Ads — paid search campaign landing pages are a different problem; see Apple Search Ads in China guide for ad-click mismatch, not Spotlight gallery copy
  • Calling the app "Search replacement" — 替代系统搜索 overclaims when the app only indexes its own content or a subset of file types
  • Implying guaranteed Spotlight placement — listing claims top Spotlight results for every query when ranking depends on system behavior and donation quality
  • Conflating listing copy with in-app search field labels — search bar placeholders and result row titles are binary localization, not Connect metadata
  • English "Find it instantly" on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in Spotlight mockups on PNG exports are still Latin
  • What's New still English after Spotlight launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when Search with Spotlight or find-it-in-Spotlight features shipped in a recent version
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement CoreSpotlight or CSSearchableItem — searchable-item indexing and NSUserActivity donation are outside listing rewrite

FAQ

Does AppLocale implement CoreSpotlight, CSSearchableItem, or NSUserActivity?

No. AppLocale rewrites App Store Connect metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, and screenshot caption lines on your zh-Hans product page. CoreSpotlight indexing, CSSearchableItem attributes, NSUserActivity donation, and in-app search UI are engineering tasks outside AppLocale scope.

How should zh-Hans listing copy talk about Spotlight without over-claiming?

Listing copy should describe the Spotlight and iOS Search flows your app actually ships — searchable from Spotlight, appears in Siri Suggestions, find it in Spotlight onboarding — without implying you replace system Search, guarantee top Spotlight placement, or index content your app does not donate. We rewrite from your English source claims; we do not invent Spotlight features your binary does not support.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Spotlight listing fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters on the zh-Hans row. The keyword field allows up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially subtitle and caption lines that must fit on-device mockups showing Spotlight search results or Siri Suggestions chips.

Spotlight listing copy covers Search with Spotlight, Find it instantly, Spotlight Search, and Siri Suggestions from Spotlight marketing on the product page. App Intents covers Ask Siri to… action phrases and Shortcuts tiles. Spoken App Shortcut phrases covers Hey Siri invocation lines. Apple Search Ads China covers paid search campaigns whose clicks land on English product pages. Those surfaces have separate listing guides.

No. On-device Spotlight, iOS Search, and Siri Suggestions at runtime come from your app binary and system ranking — not App Store Connect listing fields. AppLocale covers product-page marketing copy only.
